# Diagnostics are generated by the matching batch run, not on demand

Every Session needs a matched pair of Diagnostic Forms — the Baseline Diagnostic and the Exit Ticket — and producing them takes one Claude call of a few thousand tokens. The specification said only that they are generated "before the session," which left the actual trigger open. We generate them inside the hourly matching batch run: the same run that commits a match sweeps for upcoming scheduled sessions with no forms and fills them in. A future reader will find the matching engine making AI calls, which is surprising enough to want an explanation here.

The alternative was lazy generation on first load of the join link, which is the obvious design and the wrong one. It puts a multi-second AI call directly in front of the student, at the exact moment they are trying to enter a tutoring session, on the unreliable connection this platform exists to serve. Generating during the batch run has slack to spend instead: a request's window must be at least two hours out, and the run fires hourly, so the work happens long before anybody is waiting on it. The cost is a Claude call for sessions that later get cancelled, which is a few cents at pilot scale and cheap next to making the worst-connected student wait.

Because generation is no longer on the critical path, it is allowed to fail. A failure is swallowed, the session simply has no diagnostic, and its Delta Growth is null rather than fabricated. The next hourly sweep retries it. What a failure must never do is take down a run that has already committed real matches, which is why the generation phase runs after the matching loop and catches everything.

The sweep carries a hard ceiling of twenty generations per run. Without it, a failure mode that never resolves — a malformed microtopic, a persistently rejected schema — would produce one AI call per pending session every hour, indefinitely, on a project whose stated constraint is a near-zero budget. Anything over the cap simply waits for the next run, which costs nothing given the two-hour lead time. The same reasoning fixes the Concept Blueprint on the microtopic rather than regenerating it per session: it is one call per microtopic for the life of the product, and it is also what makes two sessions on the same microtopic measure the same five concepts, without which the tutor impact page would be averaging numbers that were never comparable.
